claims.text: The base (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation.
The base alloy has poor mechanical integrity and tends to crack.
Partial substitution of Ni with Co will improve resistance to cracking.
Partial substitution of Ni with Co will retain a high caloric response.
Arc melting followed by annealing and water quenching will ensure compositional homogeneity and favorable microstructural characteristics.
Co-for-Ni substitution will modify the crystallographic lattice.
Co-for-Ni substitution will modify the phase distribution.
The substitution-induced structural changes will produce a more ductile microstructure and optimized grain boundaries.
Introducing Co will alter the local bonding environment.
Introducing Co will stabilize a phase or microstructural feature that suppresses microcrack formation and propagation.
The proposed microstructural change will reduce stress concentrations.
An optimized Co substitution will not significantly disrupt the magnetostructural transition responsible for the caloric effect.
The Co-substituted alloy could attain a compressive strength exceeding approximately 150–152 MPa.
The caloric response of the Co-substituted alloy will remain within ±10% of the unchanged alloy's response.
Excessive Co substitution may disrupt the magnetostructural transition and reduce caloric performance.
Insufficient Co substitution may fail to produce a meaningful improvement in mechanical robustness.
